answer: A newcomer earns standing by mapping one hollow chamber in a marble quarry. They wander its passages with a measuring line, sketching every turn, and file the map with the quarry office. Two surveyors retrace the route and countersign it within ten days, checking each measurement. A copied map, a chamber claimed twice, or a measurement that does not match voids the season for everyone linked and bars their sponsor for a year. Faking a thousand identities means mapping a thousand chambers, each walked and checked in person — far costlier than one honest survey.
